overallAssessment.verdict: The anglesey.ts data file is structurally strong and well-organised with comprehensive coverage across hero content, key facts, seasons, experiences, FAQs, hidden gems, and dining. However it carries three material blockers: (1) the hero image anglesey-hero.jpg has no provenance record in the image registry and cannot be published with unknown licensing; (2) all pricing in topExperiences comes from the 'Perplexity research' source declared in the file header — AI-sourced pricing violates the no-AI-content policy and is now 16+ months old; (3) the coastal path length is stated as 140 miles in anglesey.ts but 125 miles in the anglesey-coastal-path.json itinerary — a material discrepancy requiring editorial resolution against the official IOAAC source. The markdown content (content/regions/anglesey.md) is a lighter editorial piece that is broadly consistent but treats the island differently in tone and scope.
overallAssessment.structuralQuality: HIGH — the TS data file covers hero prose, keyFacts, bestFor (10 activities), seasonGuide (4 seasons), 10 insiderTips, 12 topExperiences, 10 FAQs, 6 hiddenGems, 6 localEatsAndDrinks, and full SEO meta.
overallAssessment.factualConfidence: MEDIUM — core geography, UNESCO status, bridge dates, and general character are well-established. Pricing, some operator contact details, and the coastal path length need live verification before publishing.

area_714km2.claim: 714 km² (276 sq miles), Wales' largest island
area_714km2.verdict: VERIFIED — Isle of Anglesey County Council confirms Anglesey is 715 km² (trivial rounding difference). It is indeed the largest island in Wales and the largest island in England and Wales combined.

coastalPath_140miles.claim: 140 miles (225 km), circles the entire island in 12 sections
coastalPath_140miles.verdict: DISCREPANCY — anglesey.ts states 140 miles; data/itineraries/anglesey-coastal-path.json tagline states '125-mile loop'. The official Isle of Anglesey County Council website describes the path as 'approximately 125 miles (200 km)' in most recent documentation, while older sources (including earlier Visit Wales material) quoted 140 miles. The IOAAC updated the measured distance after re-routing in 2019.
coastalPath_140miles.action: HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED — verify current official quoted length. Recommend updating anglesey.ts to match official current IOAAC figure. The 12-section structure claim is consistent with official IOAAC materials.
coastalPath_140miles.confidence: LOW — discrepancy exists; defer to official IOAAC source

population_70000.verdict: APPROXIMATELY CORRECT — 2021 census recorded Anglesey population as 69,751. Main towns Holyhead (largest, ~13,000), Llangefni (administrative centre), Beaumaris are correctly identified.

beaumarisCastle_UNESCO.claim: Beaumaris Castle, Part of the Castles of Edward I in Gwynedd
beaumarisCastle_UNESCO.verdict: VERIFIED — Beaumaris Castle is one of four Welsh castles inscribed under 'Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd' (UNESCO WHS reference 374, inscribed 1986).

menaiSuspensionBridge_1826.claim: Thomas Telford's iconic Menai Suspension Bridge (1826)
menaiSuspensionBridge_1826.verdict: VERIFIED — The Menai Suspension Bridge was completed in January 1826, designed by Thomas Telford. The Britannia Bridge (rail/road) opened in 1850 (rebuilt after 1970 fire).

holyheadPort.verdict: NEEDS_VERIFICATION — 'second-busiest' is a frequently cited but sourcing-dependent claim. Holyhead is operated by Stena Line and Irish Ferries serving Dublin and Dun Laoghaire. Its ranking relative to Dover and Portsmouth varies by year and measurement metric.
holyheadPort.action: Either verify with current Port of Holyhead statistics or rephrase to 'one of the busiest passenger ports in the UK' to avoid a potentially outdated superlative.

welshLanguage_57percent.claim: 57% Welsh speakers, one of the most Welsh-speaking areas
welshLanguage_57percent.verdict: APPROXIMATELY CORRECT — 2021 Census data showed 59.1% of Anglesey residents could speak Welsh (down from 57.2% in 2011). The 57% figure in anglesey.ts closely matches the 2011 census. The 2021 figure is slightly higher. Anglesey consistently ranks among the top Welsh-speaking local authorities.
welshLanguage_57percent.confidence: HIGH — directionally correct; minor update recommended to reflect 2021 census figure of ~59%

redSquirrels_newborough.verdict: VERIFIED — NRW/Forestry Wales confirmed Newborough National Nature Reserve supports a red squirrel population. NRW manages the site.

puffinIsland.claim: Puffin Island off Beaumaris has a puffin colony, accessible April-July by boat
puffinIsland.verdict: CONDITIONALLY CORRECT — Puffin Island (Ynys Seiriol) historically had significant puffin populations but numbers declined sharply due to brown rat predation. The RSPB and wildlife groups have undertaken rat eradication programmes in recent years to aid recovery. Current colony size and seasonal access for boat trips should be verified against the latest Wildlife Trust of North Wales/RSPB reporting.
puffinIsland.action: HUMAN REVIEW — verify current puffin colony status on Puffin Island before publishing 'puffins off Beaumaris' as a headline claim. If numbers remain very low post-decline, the copy should reflect this honestly.
puffinIsland.confidence: MEDIUM — general character correct, current colony health uncertain

southStackSteps.verdict: COMMONLY CITED — 400 steps is the figure cited by RSPB, Visit Wales, and most travel guides. Source: RSPB South Stack reserve information. The lighthouse is managed by Trinity House; the stairs and cliff path are managed by RSPB.

darkSkyStatus.verdict: NEEDS_VERIFICATION — Multiple locations in Wales have Dark Sky Discovery Site (BSAS), Dark Sky Reserve (IDA), or Dark Sky Island designations. Anglesey itself has been promoted as good stargazing territory. The specific 'Dark Sky Discovery Site' designation should be confirmed with Dark Sky Wales / British Astronomical Society.
darkSkyStatus.action: Verify whether Anglesey holds a formal dark sky designation (site, reserve, or island status) vs. being generally described as dark sky-friendly.

llanddwynAccessNote.claim: Llanddwyn Island only accessible at low tide
llanddwynAccessNote.verdict: PARTIALLY INACCURATE — Llanddwyn is a tidal peninsula, not a true island. The narrow causeway section can be covered by high spring tides, but visitors can cross for most tidal states. NRW guidance says to check tide times for the narrowest section, but 'only accessible at low tide' overstates the restriction.
llanddwynAccessNote.action: Update copy to: 'The narrow causeway can flood at high spring tides — check tide times before walking out.' This is more accurate and avoids discouraging visits unnecessarily.
